# Side Navigation

Provide access to navigation links in your app on the left side of the page.
See [Side Navigation guidelines<i className="ds-icon-launch"></i>](https://design-system.airbus.corp/components/side-navigation/design/)

We recommend to use a permanent `Side Navigation` on desktop.<br />
When using temporary mode, the component is based on the <LinkTo kind="Components/Drawer" story="docs">Drawer</LinkTo> component. <br />
When using permanent mode, `elevation` and `headerPadding` props, are not applied.<br />
Max allowed levels is 3, we support until that and no indendation afterwards.<br />

<Source code="import { SideNav, SideNavCategory, SideNavItem, SideNavSection } from &#x22;@airbus/components-react&#x22;" />

<Primary />

<Controls />

* Any other props supplied will be provided to the `<nav>` HTML element
* For details on CSS styles, see [CSS implementation](https://github.airbus.corp/Airbus/design-system/blob/develop/packages/styles/src/elements/SideNav/index.ts)

### Multilevel navigation

Try not to use more than 3 levels of navigation.

The logic to open, close or navigate to categories can be adapted to your application needs.

In this example, opened categories collapse automatically when opening another one, and clicking on a category navigate to corresponding content.

<Canvas of={SideNavStories.Multilevel} />

In this other example users can freely open or close any category, without navigating to some category content.

<Canvas of={SideNavStories.MultilevelFree} />

### With Search Input

With complex navigation hierarchy, it can a be good practice to provide a search input at the top of the SideNav.
This example simply highlights the matching text, but it could conditionnaly render the categories and items.

<Canvas of={SideNavStories.WithSearchInput} />

```css
.side-nav-search {
    margin: 0 0.5rem 1rem;
}
```
